title: Wing Lower Cover Stringer Run-Out — Blend-Out and Bonded Strap Repair

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: Permanent repair for small fatigue indications at the wing lower cover stringer run-out on the four-engine stretched aircraft, combining blend-out of the indication with a bonded strap over the last three fastener rows.

sections.purpose: This repair removes a small fatigue indication at a lower cover stringer run-out and restores the fatigue capability of the joint with a bonded strap.
sections.damage_assessment: Size every indication found by the ultrasonic survey in both directions and record its position by stringer number and fastener number. Indications up to 6 mm in length at a single fastener, not extending into the stringer foot radius and not at the last fastener of the run-out, are inside this repair. Any indication above 6 mm, any indication at the last fastener, or indications at more than one fastener in the same run-out, are outside it and need an engineering assessment. Because this is a tank interior repair, confirm the damage extent before the aircraft is committed: a second tank entry to extend the repair costs as much as the first.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the fastener at the indication and ream the hole oversize until the indication is removed, checking with an eddy current bolt hole probe after each reaming step. Blend the hole edges. Where the indication extends into the surface, blend it out to a dish with a length to depth ratio above thirty to one and do a dye penetrant inspection of the dish. Cut the bonded strap from the stringer kit D5710124822382 material to the layout of repair drawing RD-57-10-12-005. Prepare the faying faces to the bonding standard, install the strap with the structural film adhesive and cure it under the heat blanket at the temperature and time on the drawing. CAUTION: DO NOT EXCEED THE CURE TEMPERATURE. THE LOWER COVER TEMPER IS AFFECTED ABOVE IT. Fasten the strap over the last three fastener rows into the lower spar cap kit D5710125087378 and the skin panel FA508915-80, using the oversize fastener from the kit at the reamed position. Re-clip the fuel quantity harness with loop clamps EN26865-6B clear of the strap. Restore the tank sealant over the whole repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 8 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the repaired run-out at every 2 000 flight cycles, which is half the normal survey interval. The repair does not release the aircraft from the airworthiness directive inspection of the remaining run-outs. Report every repair to Aeralis with the ultrasonic record; the fleet fatigue model is calibrated on these reports.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Indications up to 6 mm at a single fastener, not extending into the stringer foot radius and not at the last fastener of the run-out. One indication per run-out.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows over the run-out, 42 fasteners total at 24 mm pitch and 18 mm edge distance, with one oversize fastener at the reamed position

abstract: Permanent repair for small fatigue indications at the wing lower cover stringer run-out on the four-engine stretched aircraft, combining blend-out of the indication with a bonded strap over the last three fastener rows.

sections.purpose: This repair removes a small fatigue indication at a lower cover stringer run-out and restores the fatigue capability of the joint with a bonded strap, on aircraft not yet at the reinforced standard.
sections.damage_assessment: Size every indication found by the ultrasonic survey in both directions and record its position by stringer number and fastener number. Indications up to 6 mm in length at a single fastener, not extending into the stringer foot radius and not at the last fastener of the run-out, are inside this repair. Any indication above 6 mm, any indication at the last fastener, or indications at more than one fastener in the same run-out, are outside it and the aircraft must go to the reinforced standard. Because this is a tank interior repair, confirm the damage extent before the aircraft is committed: a second tank entry to extend the repair costs as much as the first.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the fastener at the indication and ream the hole oversize until the indication is removed, checking with an eddy current bolt hole probe after each reaming step. Blend the hole edges. Where the indication extends into the surface, blend it out to a dish with a length to depth ratio above thirty to one and do a dye penetrant inspection of the dish. Prepare the faying faces to the bonding standard, install the strap with the structural film adhesive and cure it under the heat blanket at the temperature and time on the drawing. Re-clip the fuel quantity harness with loop clamps EN26865-6B clear of the strap. Restore the tank sealant over the whole repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 8 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment or until the reinforced standard is embodied, whichever occurs first. Do a repeat ultrasonic inspection of the repaired run-out at every 2 000 flight cycles, which is half the normal survey interval. The repair does not release the aircraft from the airworthiness directive inspection of the remaining run-outs. Interaction with the reinforced standard: the build-up is sized on parent thickness and a clean faying surface at the same last three fastener rows this repair straps over, so the two cannot occupy one run-out. The repair design office position is that the strap is removed and the oversize hole assessed individually before the build-up is fitted; over-working the strap is not permitted, and a run-out where the oversize hole cannot be brought back inside the build-up fastener schedule takes a panel change instead. Roughly one run-out in six inboard of rib 14 carries this repair on the aircraft in the effectivity, so the survey is done before the visit is planned and not on the day. Report every repair to Aeralis with the ultrasonic record; the fleet fatigue model is calibrated on these reports.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Indications up to 6 mm at a single fastener, not extending into the stringer foot radius and not at the last fastener of the run-out. One indication per run-out.
